newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota Motor reorganises North American operations.
newsitem.headline: Toyota Motor reorganises North American operations.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Wednesday it set up a firm in the United States on October 1 to direct its North American manufacturing subsidiaries so as to speed up decision-making and improve efficiency.

The Kentucky-based new firm, Toyota Motor Manufacturing, North America Inc (TMMNA), has taken over various administrative functions previously carried out by eight Toyota subisidiaries in the United States and Canada, Toyota said in a statement.

The eight companies -- three Toyota Motor Manufacturing companies in Kentucky, Indiana and West Virginia as well as TABC Inc, Bodine Aluminum Inc, Canadian Autoparts Toyota Inc, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada Inc and New United Motor Manufacturing Inc -- are now under TMMNA's direction.
Business planning and production control from Japan, purchasing, legal/external affairs and other functions of the companies have been transferred in large part to TMMNA, the statement said.
As part of the reorganisation, Toyota set up Toyota Motor North Ameria Inc (TMA) in California as the holding company of TMMNA and Toyota Motor Sales U.S.A. Inc, its sales unit in the United States.
TMMNA's capitalisation is $1.5 billion, while that of TMA is $876 million.
The reorganisation of Toyota's North American operations will not affect its production and sales in the North American market, a company spokesman said.

Toyota wanted to simplify the structure of ownership of its North American manufacturing units as Toyota Motor Sales was the major owner of several manufacturing units, including TMMK, which was formerly named Toyota Motor Manufacturing Inc (TMM), the spokesman said.
The reorganisation will not involve any special cost, he said.
As a result of the reorganisation, TMS will own only Toyota Motor Credit Corp, based in Torrance, California.

Some business planning and production control functions for the North American market will be transferred to TMMNA from Japan, and similar functions, as well as accounting and finance, will move to it from existing North American manufacturing units.
